misconceptions.description: Uses sin θ instead of sin²θ in the maximum-height formula.
misconceptions.remediation: Maximum height comes from the vertical component only: H = (u sin θ)²/2g. The whole vertical velocity is squared, so the sine is squared too. Check: the answer's units and the θ = 90° limit (H = u²/2g).

misconceptions.description: Treats the full launch speed as if it were vertical.
misconceptions.remediation: Resolve the velocity first: u_y = u sin θ, u_x = u cos θ. Only u_y fights gravity. Draw the velocity components before writing any formula.

misconceptions.description: Swaps sin and cos when resolving the launch velocity.
misconceptions.remediation: For an angle measured from the horizontal, the vertical component is u sin θ. Sanity check: at θ = 0 the vertical component must be 0, and cos 0 = 1 fails that test.

misconceptions.description: Confuses time to reach maximum height with total time of flight.
misconceptions.remediation: u sin θ / g is only the time to the top. On level ground the flight is symmetric, so total time T = 2u sin θ / g.

misconceptions.description: Believes static friction always equals μₛN.
misconceptions.remediation: μₛN is only the *maximum* static friction. Static friction adjusts to exactly cancel the applied force until that limit is reached. First compare the applied force with μₛN.

misconceptions.description: Uses kinetic friction for a body that is not sliding.
misconceptions.remediation: Kinetic friction μₖN acts only when surfaces slide over each other. Decide first: does the body move? If the applied force is below μₛN, it doesn't, and friction is static.

misconceptions.description: Treats Coulomb force as inversely proportional to r instead of r².
misconceptions.remediation: F ∝ q₁q₂/r². Halving r multiplies F by 4, not 2. Write the ratio F'/F with every changed factor before simplifying.

misconceptions.description: Accounts for only one of several simultaneous changes.
misconceptions.remediation: When several quantities change, write F'/F = (q₁'/q₁)(q₂'/q₂)(r/r')² and fill in every factor explicitly.

misconceptions.description: Combines resistors in the wrong order (parallel before series or vice versa).
misconceptions.remediation: Redraw the circuit and find the innermost group first: resistors sharing *both* end nodes are in parallel; resistors carrying the *same current* with no junction between them are in series.

misconceptions.description: Takes terminal voltage equal to EMF when current flows.
misconceptions.remediation: When a current I flows, the terminal voltage is V = E − Ir. It equals E only on open circuit.

misconceptions.description: Equates the photon energy with the photoelectron's kinetic energy.
misconceptions.remediation: Part of the photon's energy (the work function φ) is spent freeing the electron: KEmax = hν − φ. Always subtract φ.

misconceptions.description: Thinks the period of a spring–mass system is proportional to the mass.
misconceptions.remediation: T = 2π√(m/k): the period goes as the *square root* of mass. Four times the mass gives twice the period.

misconceptions.description: Treats an adiabatic process as isothermal (temperature unchanged).
misconceptions.remediation: In an adiabatic process no heat enters, so work done on the gas raises its temperature: TV^(γ−1) = constant. Isothermal means T is constant, which needs heat exchange.

misconceptions.description: Confuses the dimensions of energy with those of Planck's constant.
misconceptions.remediation: Derive dimensions from a defining equation: E = hν, so [h] = [E]/[ν] = [ML²T⁻²]/[T⁻¹] = [ML²T⁻¹].
